name: Nutritional Bioenergetics: Energy Expenditure, Nitrogen Balance, and Malnutrition Syndromes

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd ed
clinicalPearls: Basal metabolic rate accounts for 60-75% of daily energy expenditure; respiratory quotient reflects fuel (CHO=1.0, fat=0.7)
Negative nitrogen balance occurs when urinary nitrogen excretion exceeds intake, reflecting severe catabolism in trauma and burns
Kwashiorkor results from selective protein deficiency with adequate calories, presenting with edema, fatty liver, and dermatitis
Marasmus stems from global caloric starvation, causing severe muscle and fat wasting with an alert, elderly facies and no edema
Refeeding syndrome occurs upon reintroducing carbohydrates in starvation, triggering insulin surges and fatal hypophosphatemia
reference.pathophysiology: Energy balance requires matching caloric and protein intake to basal demands and physical activity. In kwashiorkor, protein deficiency impairs hepatic apolipoprotein B-100 synthesis, blocking VLDL secretion and creating severe hepatic steatosis; concurrently, hypoalbuminemia collapses capillary oncotic pressure, producing ascites and anasarca. In starved patients, rapid carbohydrate feeding provokes insulin release, which drives phosphate, potassium, and magnesium into cells, precipitating cardiac arrest.
additionalDifferentials: Kwashiorkor vs Marasmus vs Marasmic Kwashiorkor
Cachexia of malignancy or chronic heart failure
additionalInvestigations: Serum albumin, prealbumin (transthyretin), and transferrin levels
24-Hour urinary urea nitrogen for nitrogen balance calculation
Baseline and serial serum phosphate, potassium, and magnesium during nutritional support
Liver function tests and abdominal ultrasound for hepatic steatosis in kwashiorkor
